Module proof · Mathematics alongside Lean

Discrete remainder bounds in the OBABO energy

References and publication status for this development

Published source; corrected checked proofs

The comparison uses the supplied mainDR_dec_18.tex manuscript. The results prove Wasserstein convergence of the kinetic diffusion, invariance of its Gibbs measure, KLMC and KLMC2 error estimates for correlated Gaussian increments, their Cholesky representations, and explicit iteration counts for a prescribed error. The corrected proofs are unpublished. The reference table records the correction to the continuous prefactor and the stochastic Hessian-difference terms retained in the second-order comparison. The KLMC2 estimate retains the exact fourth Gaussian moment in every dimension; the coarser displayed simplification assumes p≥2p\ge2p≥2. The stronger inverse-step-square exponential term is also proved. Continuous solutions are continuous in L2L^2L2 on finite time intervals. Almost-sure continuity of sample paths is not proved here.

  • Arnak S. Dalalyan and Lionel Riou-Durand (2020). On sampling from a log-concave density using kinetic Langevin diffusions. Bernoulli 26(3), 1956–1988. arXiv

for s=(v,x)s=(v,x)s=(v,x), s′=(v′,x′)s'=(v',x')s′=(v′,x′). This module proves the purely algebraic part of the one-step contraction of the OBABO scheme. It realises Ea,b\mathcal E_{a,b}Ea,b​ as the square of a Hilbert norm, expands the energy of a state of the form s+hA+rs+hA+rs+hA+r (Euler increment along the kinetic drift A=(−γv−F,v)A=(-\gamma v-F,v)A=(−γv−F,v) plus a remainder rrr), bounds each term, and concludes that the difference of two synchronously coupled OBABO steps contracts the energy by the factor 1−mh/(3γ)1-mh/(3\gamma)1−mh/(3γ) whenever the step satisfies 33γ3h≤m33\gamma^3h\le m33γ3h≤m, γh≤1\gamma h\le1γh≤1 and 12γ2h2≤112\gamma^2h^2\le112γ2h2≤1. The force, the damping factor δ=e−γh/2\delta=e^{-\gamma h/2}δ=e−γh/2 and the dissipativity inequality are inputs here; they are supplied from the potential in the module on OBABO contraction.

01The weighted energy as the square of a Hilbert norm §

Mathematical statement and proof

Definitions. Let H⊕2HH\oplus_2HH⊕2​H denote H×HH\times HH×H with the inner product ⟨(p,q),(p′,q′)⟩=⟨p,p′⟩+⟨q,q′⟩\langle(p,q),(p',q')\rangle=\langle p,p'\rangle+\langle q,q'\rangle⟨(p,q),(p′,q′)⟩=⟨p,p′⟩+⟨q,q′⟩ and the Euclidean norm ∥(p,q)∥2=(∥p∥2+∥q∥2)1/2\|(p,q)\|_2=(\|p\|^2+\|q\|^2)^{1/2}∥(p,q)∥2​=(∥p∥2+∥q∥2)1/2. For a,b∈Ra,b\in\mathbb Ra,b∈R define

Ta,b(v,x)=(x+bv, a−b2 v)∈H⊕2H,Na,b(s)=∥Ta,bs∥2,T_{a,b}(v,x)=\bigl(x+bv,\ \sqrt{a-b^2}\,v\bigr)\in H\oplus_2H,\qquad N_{a,b}(s)=\|T_{a,b}s\|_2,Ta,b​(v,x)=(x+bv, a−b2​v)∈H⊕2​H,Na,b​(s)=∥Ta,b​s∥2​,

where ⋅\sqrt{\cdot}⋅​ is the nonnegative square root (and y=0\sqrt y=0y​=0 for y<0y<0y<0), and let Ba,b\mathcal B_{a,b}Ba,b​ be the pairing defined above.

Claim. Assume b2≤ab^2\le ab2≤a. Then for all s,s′∈H×Hs,s'\in H\times Hs,s′∈H×H:

  1. Na,b(s)2=Ea,b(s)N_{a,b}(s)^2=\mathcal E_{a,b}(s)Na,b​(s)2=Ea,b​(s);
  2. Ba,b(s,s′)=⟨Ta,bs,Ta,bs′⟩\mathcal B_{a,b}(s,s')=\langle T_{a,b}s,T_{a,b}s'\rangleBa,b​(s,s′)=⟨Ta,b​s,Ta,b​s′⟩;
  3. Ba,b(s,s′)≤Na,b(s) Na,b(s′)\mathcal B_{a,b}(s,s')\le N_{a,b}(s)\,N_{a,b}(s')Ba,b​(s,s′)≤Na,b​(s)Na,b​(s′).

Proof. Put c=a−b2c=\sqrt{a-b^2}c=a−b2​; since a−b2≥0a-b^2\ge0a−b2≥0, c2=a−b2c^2=a-b^2c2=a−b2. (1) By the definition of the Euclidean norm, the expansion ∥x+bv∥2=∥x∥2+2b⟨x,v⟩+b2∥v∥2\|x+bv\|^2=\|x\|^2+2b\langle x,v\rangle+b^2\|v\|^2∥x+bv∥2=∥x∥2+2b⟨x,v⟩+b2∥v∥2 and ∥cv∥2=c2∥v∥2\|cv\|^2=c^2\|v\|^2∥cv∥2=c2∥v∥2,

Na,b(v,x)2=∥x∥2+2b⟨x,v⟩+b2∥v∥2+(a−b2)∥v∥2=Ea,b(v,x).N_{a,b}(v,x)^2=\|x\|^2+2b\langle x,v\rangle+b^2\|v\|^2+(a-b^2)\|v\|^2=\mathcal E_{a,b}(v,x).Na,b​(v,x)2=∥x∥2+2b⟨x,v⟩+b2∥v∥2+(a−b2)∥v∥2=Ea,b​(v,x).

(2) By bilinearity of the inner product,

⟨Ta,bs,Ta,bs′⟩=⟨x+bv,x′+bv′⟩+c2⟨v,v′⟩=⟨x,x′⟩+b⟨x,v′⟩+b⟨v,x′⟩+(b2+a−b2)⟨v,v′⟩,\langle T_{a,b}s,T_{a,b}s'\rangle=\langle x+bv,x'+bv'\rangle+c^2\langle v,v'\rangle=\langle x,x'\rangle+b\langle x,v'\rangle+b\langle v,x'\rangle+(b^2+a-b^2)\langle v,v'\rangle,⟨Ta,b​s,Ta,b​s′⟩=⟨x+bv,x′+bv′⟩+c2⟨v,v′⟩=⟨x,x′⟩+b⟨x,v′⟩+b⟨v,x′⟩+(b2+a−b2)⟨v,v′⟩,

which is Ba,b(s,s′)\mathcal B_{a,b}(s,s')Ba,b​(s,s′). (3) follows from (2) and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality in H⊕2HH\oplus_2HH⊕2​H. □\square□

Thus, when b2≤ab^2\le ab2≤a, Na,bN_{a,b}Na,b​ is a seminorm on H×HH\times HH×H whose square is the energy, and Ba,b\mathcal B_{a,b}Ba,b​ is the associated symmetric bilinear form. The Euclidean product norm is needed here: with the maximum norm on H×HH\times HH×H the square of the norm of Ta,bsT_{a,b}sTa,b​s would not be Ea,b(s)\mathcal E_{a,b}(s)Ea,b​(s).

How the Lean proof follows this argument
  1. weightedPhaseTransform a b s is WithLp.toLp 2 (s.2 + b • s.1, Real.sqrt (a - b ^ 2) • s.1). The type WithLp 2 (E × E) is the product with the ℓ2\ell^2ℓ2 (Euclidean) norm and inner product, H⊕2HH\oplus_2HH⊕2​H; WithLp.toLp 2 places a pair into it. On the plain product E × E Mathlib uses the maximum norm, which is why this type is used. weightedPhaseNorm a b s is the norm of the transform, and weightedPhasePairing a b s t is Ba,b(s,t)\mathcal B_{a,b}(s,t)Ba,b​(s,t), written with Mathlib's real inner product notation ⟪·, ·⟫; the energy weightedPhaseEnergy a b s = ‖s.2‖ ^ 2 + 2 * b * ⟪s.2, s.1⟫ + a * ‖s.1‖ ^ 2 comes from the module on the OBABO energy.
  2. weightedPhaseNorm_sq (hypothesis hab : b ^ 2 ≤ a) rewrites the norm square by WithLp.prod_norm_sq_eq_of_L2 (∥(p,q)∥22=∥p∥2+∥q∥2\|(p,q)\|_2^2=\|p\|^2+\|q\|^2∥(p,q)∥22​=∥p∥2+∥q∥2), expands ∥x+bv∥2\|x+bv\|^2∥x+bv∥2 with norm_add_sq_real, uses Real.sq_sqrt (sub_nonneg.mpr hab) for c2=a−b2c^2=a-b^2c2=a−b2, and finishes with ring.
  3. weightedPhasePairing_eq_inner expands the inner product of the transforms by WithLp.prod_inner_apply and bilinearity (inner_add_left, real_inner_smul_right, …); the coefficient identity c2⟨v,v′⟩=(a−b2)⟨v,v′⟩c^2\langle v,v'\rangle=(a-b^2)\langle v,v'\ranglec2⟨v,v′⟩=(a−b2)⟨v,v′⟩ is hs', and nlinarith closes the resulting linear identity.
  4. weightedPhasePairing_le rewrites with the previous lemma and applies Cauchy–Schwarz, real_inner_le_norm.

  2. weightedPhaseEnergy_add_le uses weightedPhasePairing_le (hp) and the square hs (N(s)−N(t))2≥0(N(s)-N(t))^2\ge0(N(s)−N(t))2≥0, rewritten by weightedPhaseNorm_sq; nlinarith adds them.

The hypotheses of (1) and (2) are explicit norm bounds on the force and on the components of the remainder; they are verified for the OBABO step in the last step of this module.

How the Lean proof follows this argument
  1. In obabo_drift_energy_bound, hequiv is the metric equivalence weightedPhaseEnergy_equiv with the coefficient condition obabo_metric_condition γ L hγ hL hfriction; hbase is the first inequality of (∗)(\ast)(∗). hid is the identity for L E(A)L\,\mathcal E(A)LE(A), proved by expanding and field_simp/ring. hc is γ−L/γ≥0\gamma-L/\gamma\ge0γ−L/γ≥0, hi the Cauchy–Schwarz bound, hn replaces γ−L/γ\gamma-L/\gammaγ−L/γ by γ\gammaγ, and hsq, hlinear are the bounds on ∥F∥2\|F\|^2∥F∥2 and 2γ∥v∥∥F∥2\gamma\|v\|\|F\|2γ∥v∥∥F∥ from hforce. The hint terms hyoungScaled (153256L(γ∥x∥−2∥v∥)2≥0\frac{153}{256}L(\gamma\|x\|-2\|v\|)^2\ge0256153​L(γ∥x∥−2∥v∥)2≥0), hLX and hLV (multiples of γ2−4L≥0\gamma^2-4L\ge0γ2−4L≥0) are exactly the three estimates of the proof, and nlinarith combines them into hraw. hfinal multiplies by (∗)(\ast)(∗), and mul_le_mul_iff_right₀ hL cancels the factor L>0L>0L>0.
  2. In obabo_remainder_energy_bound the remainder is a pair r : E × E with r.1 the velocity and r.2 the position component; hposition and hvelocity are the two hypotheses. hRupper is the second inequality of (∗)(\ast)(∗); hpSq, hvSq square the hypotheses with sq_le_sq₀, and hpBound, hvBound apply (p+q)2≤2p2+2q2(p+q)^2\le2p^2+2q^2(p+q)2≤2p2+2q2 through the squares hpSum, hvSum. hcX and hcV are the two coefficient inequalities, derived from 4L≤γ24L\le\gamma^24L≤γ2 (hLG, hLsq). hraw collects everything by nlinarith only […], and the final division by LLL is as in the first lemma.
